text:
maya: Pushed the mini-window formation threshold tweak at 03:00 UTC (reduce from 32 tokens -> 16 tokens) to improve small-req throughput. Seeing a tail latency jump for sub-64-token requests.
maya: 95p went from ~120ms -> ~420ms in the last hour. Rollback? :thinking_face:
deploy-bot: deploy/continuous-batcher v3.4.1 promoted to prod by maya at 03:00 UTC
sam: ugh, saw that on the dashboard. Throughput is fine but p95 latency spike correlates with the rollout window.
sam: any quick profiler traces? can we see which path is hot (slow-path vs fast-path)?
lee: grabbing a few pprof snapshots now. Initial glance: a lot more time in kernel-selection and batch-assembly code.
lee: snippet from the trace (aggregated):
```
25% batch_assembly::coalesce
20% kernel_router::choose_kernel
18% kv_cache::lookup_or_prefetch
12% grpc_send
... rest noise
```
maya: interesting that kv_cache lookup rose — we didn't touch cache keys. The threshold change probably changed batch composition which changed cache locality.
devon: I replayed a few requests with the new threshold in staging. Observed lots of smaller micro-batches forming and then getting merged mid-queue causing extra scheduling churn.
ash: do we have the queue policy logs? maybe the q-limit / q-time interplay is causing requeueing.
sam: pulled queue metrics: requeue rate spiked ~3x after rollout, avg queue depth per worker decreased but requeue attempts increased. Looks like more tiny batches that then time out and re-enter.
lee: also saw kernel selection toggling between fastpath (vectorized) and fallback scalar kernel more often. The cost-model is sensitive to batch shape; the smaller batches push some shapes to fallback.
maya: hypothesis: lowering mini-window threshold increases frequency of short-lived batches that exceed token budget but are small in batch size, causing kernel-selection oscillation + kv-cache misses -> tail latency.
ash: can we test increasing token_budget_target or bumping window merge timeout? quick AB in prod for a subset.
devon: started a canary route with window_merge.timeout bumped from 8ms -> 16ms for 10% of traffic.
ops-bot: canary route started (10%) via routing policy 'mini-window-slowfix' at 03:22 UTC
sam: early canary metrics look promising: p95 for canary ~150ms vs 420ms for rest. requeue rate down too.
ash: nice. That suggests merge timeout avoids churn. But need to validate unit-cost impact.
lee: profiling canary side: kernel selection stabilizes (80% fastpath), kv_cache hit-rate up ~4%. Good sign.
maya: do we want to roll this to all? we should also consider adjusting cost model so kernel-selection doesn't flip on tiny changes.
ash: agree. Plan: (1) promote merge timeout bump cluster-wide, (2) adjust token_budget_target + add hysteresis to kernel cost comparison, (3) run synthetic workload to measure unit token cost delta.
sam: I'll open a short RFC for the kernel hysteresis change; devon/lee can include profiling experiments.
ash: rollout note: when promoting, watch p95, requeue_rate, kernel_fallback_rate, and unit token cost over next 2 hours.
maya: rolling merge timeout to 100% now (promote canary), doing staged by region.
deploy-bot: rolling update started for deploy/continuous-batcher v3.4.1-hotfix at 03:40 UTC by maya
ash: also adding a short-term alert: if requeue_rate > 2x baseline AND p95 > 200ms, auto-snapshot traces for 5m.
sam: after full roll, p95 returned to ~130ms. unit token cost +2% (expected) but acceptable.
lee: leaving the kernel cost-hysteresis work in a branch; will run A/B in a controlled window next week.
maya: thanks all. Lesson: mini-window threshold interacts nonlinearly with merge timeout, kv-cache locality, and kernel cost model. Need integrated test harness for small-batch workload permutations. :white_check_mark:
ash: filed follow-ups: #1234 integrated small-batch perf harness, #1235 kernel hysteresis RFC, #1236 cost-analysis job to quantify tradeoffs.
maya: closing this thread; reopen if any regressions pop.
